guide: Start here: open Start and type the household name, both partner names and the agreed share of partner 1 in the yellow cells.
Replace demo data, step 1: clear the demo rows of Shared costs, Income, Kids costs and Allowances, keep the header row, and keep Team as your own contacts.
Replace demo data, step 2: in Settle up type one row for each complete month with its date; the totals fill in by themselves from Shared costs.
Replace demo data, step 3: type your own plan and cut shares in Lose one income, your debts in Rate change and your numbers in Scenario inputs.
Pay-day routine: when a paycheck or client payment arrives, type it in Income; check the Transfer to Joint tool and set your standing transfer.
Weekly routine: type every shared cost with who paid it, pay the allowance on its day and type it in Allowances with the saved part.
Month-close routine, in this order: type the last shared costs, read Fair split by month, run Settle Up, make the payment, type the date in Settled on, then read Over-paid streak.
Scenario routine: change a value in Scenario inputs, then run the Lose One Income Test, the Expense Shock Test, the Interest-rate Change Test, the New Baby Plan and the Mortgage Switch Scenario.
A single adult with one income and no children can use the kids and scenario sheets and leave partner 2 and the shared cost rows empty.
Use the 18 tools, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details written in.
Every verdict is an estimate from your numbers; any range shown is a typical range, check your own numbers.

Why a workbook: one flat price, no yearly renewal, your data stays with you and there is nothing to link or re-connect; you type or paste your own data. It works in Excel and Google Sheets with no macros.
What this is not: it is not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice.

listing.title: Partners, Kids and Shared Costs Excel Template: Fair Split, Settle Up, Allowances, Scenario Tests, Household Budget
listing.headline: Split shared costs fairly and test what if an income stops
listing.description:
Run the money between two partners and the children in one Excel workbook, for a couple, a family or a single adult with children. Type your shared costs with who paid and the workbook shows the fair split by month, what each partner should pay against what each paid, and who owes whom. Settle Up nets the open months into one payment, the Running Balance carries what is still owed and the Over-paid Streak Check shows when one partner paid above the agreed share month after month.

The Fair-split Calculator compares an equal split, an income share and a custom share, the Income Share tool follows take-home pay, and the Transfer to Joint tool gives each partner's monthly amount and the amount for each payday. Kids Costs by Child and Year add up childcare, school, activities, clothing and allowance against your own plan, and the Allowance Planner and Saved Check follow what each child saves.

Scenario tests answer the what-ifs: lose one income, a cut list that closes the gap, an expense shock against your emergency fund, an interest-rate change debt by debt, a new baby plan and a mortgage switch with your own numbers.

18 tools, 12 printable sheets, 12 documents, 12 checklists and 34 ready text messages to partners, the children, the grandparent, the school office and your bank branch are included. This is part seven of the Household Finance suite. A standard .xlsx workbook that works in Excel and Google Sheets, with no macros, no subscription and no bank links: you type or paste your own data. It is a household money kit, not a bank app, and not tax, legal, investment or credit advice. Every verdict is an estimate from your own numbers.
